title: Tesla's Missing Autopilot Data Showed It Detected A Hazard Before Fatal Crash, Despite Claims It Was Missing

reading.body:
A Tesla vehicle operating on Autopilot was involved in a fatal crash. Tesla told the family that crash data from the vehicle was not available. A security researcher later demonstrated that the data had been retained in the vehicle all along, contrary to Tesla's assertion to the family.

The failure occurred in how Tesla represented what information its systems possessed and retained. A jury ordered Tesla to pay more than $240 million in the case, and a judge upheld that verdict. What would have caught this: Tesla checking its own vehicles' data retention before making claims about what information existed, or the family's legal team having early access to independent technical analysis of the vehicle's actual capabilities.

It is not established whether Tesla's statement to the family reflected a genuine misunderstanding of the vehicle's data retention, a failure to check before responding, or any other cause.
